title: lichend uses attacker-controlled shared /tmp security state
description: Security review finding: simulator mode hard-codes state_root=/tmp/lichen. FileStorage follows a pre-existing directory and predictable key/temp paths without ownership, mode, file-type, or symlink checks; writes use create+truncate on <key>.tmp. Another local user can precreate /tmp/lichen, inject id.seed/trust/replay files, read the generated identity, or place symlinks at predictable temp paths (particularly dangerous if lichend runs privileged for TUN). All simulator instances also collide on one identity/state namespace. Use a per-user/per-instance mkdtemp/XDG runtime directory with 0700 ownership, openat-style O_NOFOLLOW/O_EXCL regular-file checks, and explicit cleanup/instance IDs; never place production credentials in a shared predictable /tmp path.
